question.problem:
Determine the range of $f(x)=\frac{3}{5}\sqrt{x-3}+3.$

The range is $f(x)$
{{field-1}}{{field-2}}.
question.worked_solution:
The range of $\sqrt{x}$ is

$$
\sqrt{x}\ge 0.
$$

Horizontal shifts do not affect the range. Hence,

$$
\sqrt{x-3}\ge 0.
$$

Multiplying the above inequality by $\frac{3}{5}$ and then adding $3,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\sqrt{x-3} & \ge 0 \\ \frac{3}{5}\sqrt{x-3} & \ge 0 \\ \frac{3}{5}\sqrt{x-3}+3 & \ge 3 \\ f(x) & \ge 3.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the range of the given function is $f(x)\in [3,\infty ).$

We can also see that this is true from the graph of the function. The graph of $y=f(x)$ is shown below.
